Birth control options

Counsel offers a range of birth control options. Below are some of the most common and cost-effective choices, and you’re always able to select alternative brand-name or generic medications if you prefer.

Tri-Lo-Sprintec

Tri-Lo-Sprintec is a daily birth control pill that uses estrogen and progestin to prevent pregnancy.

How to use
Take one pill by mouth at the same time daily. Each pack contains 21 active pills and 7 placebo pills.
Effectiveness
Over 99% effective with perfect use.
With insurance
$0 with most plans
Without insurance
From $10/month*

Loestrin Fe 1/20

Loestrin Fe 1/20 is a daily birth control pill that uses estrogen and progestin to prevent pregnancy.

How to use
Take one pill by mouth at the same time daily. Each pack contains 21 active pills and 7 iron tablets (placebo pills).
Effectiveness
Over 99% effective with perfect use.
With insurance
$0 with most plans
Without insurance
From $15/month*

Nuvaring

Nuvaring is a flexible vaginal ring that releases estrogen and progestin to prevent pregnancy.

How to use
Insert the flexible ring into the vagina. It’s worn for three weeks, then removed for one week each month.
Effectiveness
Over 99% effective with perfect use.
With insurance
$0 with most plans
Without insurance
From $30/month*

Micronor

Micronor is a daily birth control pill that uses progestin to prevent pregnancy, also called a “mini-pill”.

How to use
Take one pill by mouth at the same time daily. Each pack contains 28 active pills and no placebo pills.
Effectiveness
Over 99% effective with perfect use.
With insurance
$0 with most plans
Without insurance
From $10/month*
Birth control pills can help with

Migraines, acne, PMS, endometriosis, PCOS, period cramps and PMDD.

Patient stories

Your questions, answered

How effective is hormonal birth control?

When used perfectly—meaning no missed pills or delays—hormonal birth control is over 99% effective. With typical use, which accounts for the occasional missed pill or late refill, it’s about 91% effective. Using reminders or longer-acting options can help boost real-world effectiveness.

How does hormonal birth control prevent pregnancy?

Hormonal birth control uses hormones similar to those your body already makes to stop ovulation, thicken cervical mucus so sperm can’t reach an egg, and thin the uterine lining. Together, these effects make pregnancy much less likely when used as directed.

Are there benefits beyond preventing pregnancy?

Yes. Hormonal birth control is often prescribed to help manage acne, regulate cycles, reduce painful periods, and treat conditions like endometriosis or PCOS. These benefits can be just as important as birth control itself.

What if I have side effects or want to switch methods?

Side effects are usually mild and often improve within the first few months. If something doesn’t feel right, you can talk to your Counsel provider about trying a different option.
